source.title: The primate basal ganglia: parallel and integrative networks.

confidence_rationale: High-quality primate anatomical synthesis from a leading basal-ganglia neuroanatomist. It supports ARC-110's loop-channel decomposition (it accepts the parallel limbic/cognitive/motor circuits as the starting point) while explicitly qualifying the strict-segregation reading: the striato-nigro-striatal and thalamo-cortico-thalamic networks carry DIRECTIONAL information across circuits, channelling limbic -> cognitive -> motor. This is exactly the mapping caveat ARC-110 needs, so it is high-value even though its net direction is 'mixed' rather than pure support. Confidence 0.78: source quality strong, mapping fidelity good for the cross-talk caveat, but the directionality is an anatomical inference about information flow rather than a measured selection effect.
failure_signatures: Pure-segregation implementations (fully independent per-loop arenas with zero cross-channel routing) are NOT what the primate substrate does: Haber documents non-reciprocal feedforward connections that move information limbic -> cognitive -> motor, so an ARC-110 build that hard-partitions the loops would diverge from biology.

If the integrative spiral is the mechanism by which motivation reaches motor output, then segregation alone may not relieve F-dominance unless the post-within-loop arbitration preserves a directional limbic->motor influence -- i.e., the benefit could depend on the integration stage, not just the separation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Primate cortico-basal ganglia circuits are organised as parallel limbic, cognitive (associative), and motor pathways, BUT two anatomical networks -- the striato-nigro-striatal network and the thalamo-cortico-thalamic network -- contain non-reciprocal feedforward links that move information ACROSS functional circuits in a directional cascade (limbic -> cognitive -> motor), so action decision-making is influenced by motivational and cognitive inputs rather than running in isolated channels.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-110's decomposition into motor/associative/limbic loops is biologically warranted, but the brain does NOT run them as fully isolated arenas: there is a directional integration stage that lets the limbic 'is this worth committing to' computation propagate into the motor channel. For REE this argues that segregated loops should be coupled by a constrained, directional (limbic->cognitive->motor) routing step rather than arbitrated as N independent competitions -- and that the F-dominance relief ARC-110 predicts may depend on getting that integration stage right, not merely on splitting the arena.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Haber's directional cascade is inferred from primate tract-tracing anatomy (connection topography), not from a causal selection experiment showing that the spiral changes which action is committed. Mapping the anatomical 'information can flow this way' onto REE's 'limbic value reaches the committed action' is a functional interpretation of structure. The cascade direction (limbic->motor) is also the opposite of a naive 'keep F out of the limbic loop' reading, so it constrains rather than simply endorses the segregation design.
mapping.source_context: Review of primate (macaque) anatomical tract-tracing; circuit topography and directionality of cortico-striatal and striato-nigro-striatal projections. No behaving-agent or lesion-selection data.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (authoritative primate neuroanatomy). Mapping fidelity good specifically for the integration caveat ARC-110 must respect. Transfer risk moderate-to-high: anatomical directionality -> functional selection influence is an interpretive step, and the analogy from primate spiral to an RL selection head is structural.
